Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Daffodil-field persistence: AP-1 occupancy after stimulus withdrawal
ideas.description: Like a crowd of daffodils that stays after the breeze passes, test whether AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding and chromatin accessibility stay at enhancers days to weeks after a transient stimulus (e.g., serum, TPA, or injury) is removed. Use time-course CUT&RUN/ATAC-seq on primed versus naive cells, and compare the sites with the persistent H3K27ac and accessibility that mark memory.

ideas.title: Acute degradation to separate maintenance from initiation
ideas.description: Prime cells, then use a degron (dTAG/AID) or dominant-negative A-FOS to remove AP-1 either during priming or after it. Re-challenge the cells and measure the transcriptional recall response by RNA-seq. If memory needs AP-1 only at initiation, the primed state should persist after later removal. If AP-1 is needed to maintain it, the state should collapse.

ideas.title: Single-cell live imaging of AP-1 dynamics and recall
ideas.description: Image endogenously tagged JUN/FOS, or AP-1 reporters, in single cells through repeated stimulations, as if tracking each flower in the field in the breeze. Test whether a cell's past AP-1 activity predicts the amplitude or speed of its later response, and whether lineage or sister-cell correlations persist across divisions.

ideas.title: Pioneer-like enhancer priming with sequential stimulation and motif mutagenesis
ideas.description: Use CRISPR to mutate AP-1 motifs, or to dCas9-block them, at selected enhancers. Then test whether first-versus-second-stimulus responses, such as faster or stronger induction of nearby genes, depend on those motifs. Pair this with nucleosome-remodeling readouts (BAF/SWI-SNF recruitment, MNase) to show that AP-1 itself opens and holds the sites.

ideas.title: Synthetic AP-1 memory switch and sufficiency test
ideas.description: Transiently express or optogenetically activate AP-1 in naive cells. Then ask whether this alone creates a self-sustaining, heritable accessible state, and whether it persists through cell divisions with mitotic bookmarking (live-cell and mitotic-chromosome ChIP). Model the results with feedback-loop equations, such as JUN autoregulation, to predict bistability and hysteresis, and test the predictions by titrating the stimulus dose up and then down.
